newsitem.title: USA: Rebound in early September aluminum orders - Spector.
newsitem.headline: Rebound in early September aluminum orders - Spector.

text.p: Aluminum mill product orders in the fist half of September have recovered sharply, hard on the heels of twice upwardly revised August orders, industry analyst Stewart Spector said.

"Aluminum mill product orders in the first half of September have blasted off into the outer space," Spector said. "Whether or not the pace could be maintained for the month as a whole, September bookings could well be above September 1995 and last month."
LME three months aluminum prices tumbled to a 2-1/4 year low of $1,387 per tonne, with final business on Monday at $1,392 per tonne, down $20 from Friday.

Month-to-date, the daily booking rate is tracking up 22 percent from the daily rate for September 1995. Non-cansheet bookings in the first half of the month were running up 33 percent from September 1995, and well above the average rate for all of 1994.
Spector estimated that the daily booking rate in the first half of September was 34 million pounds of sheet and plate, and 16.7 million pounds of can sheet, and 18.4 million pounds of other products.

"The rebound in U.S. physical demand looks as if it is starting to build some strong upside momentum," Spector said. "In the meantime look for poor third quarter earnings-per-share comparisons from aluminum companies."
